rulers.name: Du Wenxiu (Sultan Sulayman)
rulers.title: Generalissimo, Sultan of Dali
rulers.note: Proclaimed generalissimo on 23 October 1856 after the Hui took Dali; 'reigned for 16 years'; infobox reign ends 26 December 1872, when he was beheaded in Dali. History of Yunnan: 'ruled 1856 - 26 December 1872'.

correction.text: Dali and its lake basin, the base of the rebellion

keyframe_review.note: 341,824 km2 for 1856-58 against a rebel state whose only named seat is Dali ('After the Hui rebels took control of Dali, Du Wenxiu was proclaimed as their generalissimo on 23 October 1856'). Cliopatria's shape is as large as the whole of Yunnan; the pages describe a power based in western Yunnan, so the shape is cut to the Dali basin. The Panthay Rebellion infobox gives no area, so the area check is by the pages' words: not a province-wide state.

keyframe_review.note: 408,545 km2 for 1859-67 (bbox east to 107.7 E and north to 31.6 N, i.e. into Guizhou and Sichuan): too large. History of Yunnan: the rebels were 'based in western Yunnan'; 'The sultanate reached the high-water mark of their power and glory in 1860'; Father Ponsot saw the Hui controlling 'almost all the towns around Zhongdian, Heqing and Lijiang' in 1863-68 (Du Wenxiu page). Kunming was attacked and sacked several times but was held by Ma Rulong for the Qing from 1862 (Ma Rulong page). The peak is dated 1860, one year after Cliopatria's change.

keyframe_review.note: 341,824 km2 for 1868-70: 'The Sultanate's power declined after 1868' (History of Yunnan) but the pages name no town lost before 1871. The Sladen mission stayed at Momien (Tengyue) from May to July 1868 (Panthay Rebellion page), so the western Yunnan shape is kept, with Tengchong added as my reading.

correction.text: Dali and the lake basin around it, the last rebel stronghold until December 1872

keyframe_review.note: 341,824 km2 for 1871-72: 'By 1871' the Qing were directing a campaign to annihilate the Yunnan Hui (History of Yunnan); on 25 December 1872 'thousands of Qing troops encircled Dali' (Du Wenxiu page). No page names the towns lost in 1871-72, so the shape is cut to the Dali region, the last stronghold.

region.text: Dali, which the Hui rebels took in 1856 and made their capital

ledger.note: 1856: the Hui of Yunnan take Dali and proclaim Du Wenxiu generalissimo. 'After the Hui rebels took control of Dali, Du Wenxiu was proclaimed as their generalissimo on 23 October 1856.' The rebellion followed an 1856 massacre of Muslims at Kunming (month not given).

ledger.note: 1860: the Sultanate reaches its peak in western Yunnan. 'The sultanate reached the high-water mark of their power and glory in 1860'; from 1860 to 1868 the rebels 'had either taken or destroyed forty towns and one hundred villages' (Panthay Rebellion page). The towns are not named; the region is my reading from Father Ponsot's list for 1863-68.

ledger.note: 1871: the Qing campaign to destroy the Hui of Yunnan is under way. 'By 1871, it was directing a campaign for the annihilation of the obdurate Hui Muslims of Yunnan'; Ma Shenglin was killed by a mortar in 1871 (Panthay Rebellion page). The page gives no campaign start and no towns.

ledger.note: 1872: Qing troops encircle Dali on 25 December. 'The Qing eventually battled their way to Dali and on December 25, 1872; thousands of Qing troops encircled Dali.'

region.text: Dali and the last rebel land in western Yunnan, retaken by the Qing

ledger.note: 1872: Du Wenxiu is beheaded at Dali and the Sultanate ends. He decided to surrender the next morning; his reign ends 26 December 1872 (infobox). The Panthay Rebellion page says Dali 'was captured by Imperial troops in January 1873' and the infobox gives the revolt as 1856-1873; the Du page says 'The revolt ended in 1873'.

wars.outcome: Qing victory: Dali fell in December 1872 or January 1873 (the pages differ), Du Wenxiu was beheaded; about one million dead.
wars.note: In 1872 Du's adopted son Prince Hassan went to England seeking recognition; Britain was courteous but refused intervention (Hassan Mission). The Sladen mission stayed at Momien (Tengyue), May to July 1868.

certainty.note: A rebel state whose land the pages name only by its towns (Dali, Lijiang, Zhongdian, Heqing, Tengyue); no boundary is given. Kunming changed hands several times without dates.

notes: Page budget (5) spent on the main article, Du Wenxiu, Ma Rulong (a disambiguation page, wasted), Ma Rulong (Qing general) and History of Yunnan; Cen Yuying (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cen_Yuying) did not load. Cliopatria's shapes (341,824 to 408,545 km2) are as large as the whole of Yunnan and in 1859-67 reach into Guizhou and Sichuan: all four are adjusted to western Yunnan from the pages' words (Dali basin 1856-58, Dali/Lijiang/Zhongdian/Heqing 1859-67, plus Tengyue 1868-70, Dali alone 1871-72). The infobox gives no area. Not on the pages: the dates of the rebel conquest of Yongchang (Baoshan), Chuxiong, Lijiang, Tengyue, the Qing recapture of Kunming, and the Qing counter-offensive towns; the dates of Kunming's changes of hands (rebels stormed it after Ma Rulong left, no year). The Panthay page is inconsistent on Dali's capture (1856 and 1857). The seed lists Kingdom of Luang Phrabang as a neighbour 1856-1872: no page opened mentions a border event there. Qing dynasty is written by ea-08-b.
